title: Structural dynamics of substrate processing by the p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 machinery
task: Elucidate ubiquitin chain coordination and substrate processing by p97-Ufd1-Npl4-FAF1 complex
key_results: Cryo-EM at near-atomic resolution traces initiator ubiquitin from Npl4 groove to ATPase channel; FAF1 helix and Ufd1-UT3 domain engage proximal ubiquitins with adaptive plasticity matching spiral staircase motor dynamics
comments: High-resolution visualization of ubiquitin routing through multi-subunit machine is notable, though dynamic transitions during substrate unfolding cycles remain partially unresolved.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Npl4 tower undergoes adaptive conformational changes responding to ATPase motor dynamics
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by cryo-EM showing Npl4 responsiveness to spiral staircase configuration changes

hypotheses.hypothesis: FAF1 and Ufd1-UT3 domains provide structural plasticity to coordinate ubiquitin delivery to Npl4
hypotheses.result: Supported by structural data showing FAF1 helix and Ufd1-UT3 engagement with proximal ubiquitins enabling smooth substrate progression

title: Structure and function of cyanobacterial Omp85 reveal Toc159/Toc90 as a chloroplast protein import pore
task: Determine how bacterial Omp85 evolved into chloroplast protein import channel Toc75
key_results: Cryo-EM reveals cyanobacterial Omp85 16-β-strand barrel with lidded structure and three POTRA-domains; Toc75–Toc90M complex mirrors Omp85–substrate intermediate with basic patch stabilizing lateral pore for import
comments: Elegant mechanistic explanation for functional divergence from export to import via substrate locking, though in vivo import validation through the reconstituted pore would strengthen claims.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Toc75–Toc90M complex structure corresponds to an Omp85–substrate assembly intermediate
hypotheses.result: Confirmed by cryo-EM structural comparison and demonstration that Toc90M functions as Omp85 substrate

hypotheses.hypothesis: Bacterial export mechanism was repurposed for protein import by stabilizing substrate assembly
hypotheses.result: Supported by identification of basic patch anchoring Toc90M and provision of lateral import conduit

title: Exosome-induced ferroptosis mediates cochlear hair cell injury via GPX4 suppression and iron overload
task: Determine mechanism of VS-derived exosome-induced ferroptosis in cochlear hair cells
key_results: VS-Exos promote ferroptosis via GPX4 downregulation and iron accumulation; Fer-1 treatment preserves auditory function in vivo
comments: Well-motivated study linking exosomal signaling to ferroptotic pathways, though causality between GPX4 suppression and hearing loss requires functional validation with GPX4 manipulation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: VS-Exos induce ferroptosis in cochlear hair cells through GPX4 suppression and iron dyshomeostasis
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PH-Exos caused greater damage than GH-Exos; Fer-1 protected hair cells

title: Targeting NAT10 alleviates granulosa cells oxidative stress and follicular atresia by disrupting ac4C acetylation of Tnc
task: Determine NAT10-catalyzed ac4C acetylation role in granulosa cell oxidative stress and follicular atresia via Tnc
key_results: NAT10 ac4C-modifies Tnc mRNA enhancing stability; Tnc inhibits Parkin-mediated mitophagy; Remodelin (NAT10 inhibitor) promotes mitophagy and improves reproductive efficiency in vivo
comments: Identifies novel epigenetic-metabolic link in follicular atresia; Remodelin shows therapeutic promise but selectivity over other NAT proteins and acetylation sites requires validation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: NAT10-catalyzed ac4C modification of Tnc mRNA stabilizes Tnc, which inhibits Parkin mitophagy and promotes GC oxidative stress and follicular atresia
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; Remodelin reverses pathway in vitro and in vivo; inhibition of NAT10 restores mitophagy and reduces atresia in fertility models

hypotheses.hypothesis: R-Spondin acts as dynamic amplifier of Wnt signaling oscillations during somitogenesis

task: Evaluate osteogenic differentiation and antibacterial activity of Vitex negundo leaf aqueous extract
key_results: VNL-AE enhanced alkaline phosphatase (2.41→2.58 fold) and mineralized matrix (0.44→3.14 fold) at 200 µg/mL; antibacterial MIC 25-100 µg/mL against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa

title: FTO-mediated m6A regulation modulates hepatic stellate cell activation through the IGF2BP1–TRIB3 axis and mitochondrial homeostasis
task: Determine FTO-mediated m6A regulation of hepatic stellate cell activation through IGF2BP1-TRIB3 axis
key_results: FTO deficiency elevated m6A methylation and TRIB3 via IGF2BP1-dependent mechanism; promoted HSC activation and collagen deposition in BDL mice

outputs: HSC activation markers (α-SMA, Col I, TGF-β)

title: Altered cellular phenotypes and a limited yet inflammation-focused transcriptional response induced by dexamethasone in caprine dermal papilla cells
task: Determine dexamethasone effects on dermal papilla cell phenotype and transcriptional response
key_results: High-dose dexamethasone reduced metabolic activity/proliferation, increased apoptosis, skewed S-phase; 373 DEGs identified with inflammation-predominant downregulation and cholesterol biosynthesis upregulation
comments: Comprehensive transcriptomic characterization reveals limited yet targeted GC response in caprine DPCs; cholesterol biosynthesis enrichment may indicate metabolic reprogramming but causal link to depilatory effects unclear.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dexamethasone suppresses DPC function and hair cycling via GR-mediated inflammatory suppression and metabolic remodeling

title: Matrigel scaffold, alone or with human placenta-derived mesenchymal stromal cells, improves histological repair of murine excisional wounds
task: Evaluate efficacy of Matrigel scaffold with hPMSCs for cutaneous wound healing in mice
key_results: Matrigel + hPMSCs achieved 86.1% collagen density vs 45.1% vehicle control at day 21; Matrigel alone contributed 80-93% of improvement
comments: Important limitation acknowledged: no non-MSC cellular control prevents attribution of benefit specifically to hPMSC identity; incremental cell contribution modest (5.8-8.3% points).

hypotheses.hypothesis: hPMSCs + Matrigel improves wound healing better than either component alone
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; combination showed highest re-epithelialization and organized architecture, but Matrigel alone drove most collagen improvement

title: The secretory peptidase inhibitor R3HDML fine-tunes p38 MAPK signaling to maintain glomerular basement membrane architecture during renal aging and disease

comments: Cell-type-specific mechanism identified; renal function preserved despite GBM architectural disruption, suggesting compensatory mechanisms or redundant structural roles.

hypotheses.hypothesis: R3HDML fine-tunes p38 MAPK signaling to maintain normal GBM composition and podocyte architecture during aging and disease
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; R3hdml loss increases p38 phosphorylation and collagen IV deposition; GBM architecture disrupted but renal function largely preserved in aging and DN models
